name: SRM Contractors
story: SRM builds roads, tunnels and slope-stabilisation works, mostly in the Himalayan belt for agencies like NHIDCL and BRO, and now in national packages. Revenue doubled in FY26 because a handful of large awards started executing. The story works if it keeps winning tunnel and hill-road work where few contractors qualify, and turns its booked profit into cash.
pe_case: Thesis: a sub-Rs 1,000 Cr contractor growing ~90% in a niche where incumbents are shrinking, at ~8x earnings. Value levers: working-capital discipline (retention, receivables), a better bid mix toward tunnels, and a credit rating upgrade to cut bank-guarantee costs. Exit: re-rating to sector multiples as scale proves out, or a strategic sale to a larger EPC player wanting hill and tunnel capability. Must-do diligence: contract-asset and receivable ageing, arbitration claims, and tunnel cost-overrun history.

name: Frontier Springs
story: Frontier makes the springs that sit under Indian railway coaches and wagons: coil, forged and the new air springs for Vande Bharat. Earnings rose 77% because railway rolling-stock production surged and air springs carry better prices. The story works if Indian Railways keeps buying at this pace and Frontier keeps its approved-vendor edge.
pe_case: Thesis: a 27%-EBITDA niche supplier with an FY27 guide of Rs 500 Cr revenue (+55%). Value levers: diversify into auto, CV and metro suspension, and professionalise tender pricing. Exit: strategic acquirers in suspension (domestic or global rail-component groups), or index inclusion. Must-do diligence: RDSO approval list and competitor count, payment days from the production units, and verified CFO.

name: Gandhi Special Tubes
story: Gandhi Special Tubes makes small, high-precision steel tubes and nuts for fuel-injection and hydraulic systems, a niche the big mills don't bother with. It earns ~40% operating margins but grows ~10% a year, so it hands the cash back through dividends and buybacks. The story is steady compounding, not a growth story.
pe_case: Thesis: a debt-free, ~41%-margin niche at ~14x, half its peer multiple. A PE fund would buy it for yield and capital return, not growth. Value levers: lever up modestly for a bigger buyback, and add adjacent precision products. Exit: a strategic sale to an auto tier-1 or tube group, or ongoing buybacks. Must-do diligence: profit split between operations and treasury income, customer concentration, and EV-transition exposure (fuel-injection lines).

name: Dynamic Cables
story: Dynamic Cables makes power cables and conductors that state power-distribution companies buy to upgrade their networks under the RDSS scheme. Profit grew 30% in FY26 and the order book covers about eight months. The story works while discoms keep spending; it weakens if the RDSS money slows after 2026.
pe_case: Thesis: a B2B cable maker at ~19x, a third below peers, with H1 FY27 profit tracking above FY26. Value levers: export and railway diversification, branded retail wires for better margins, and working-capital control on discom receivables. Exit: consolidation (large cable makers buying capacity) or index inclusion. Must-do diligence: discom receivable days, the reason bank ratings were withdrawn, and RDSS order pipeline after FY27.

name: Gulshan Polyols
story: Gulshan turns grain into ethanol for the oil companies' blending programme, alongside sorbitol and starch. Profit jumped 332% in FY26 as its new distilleries filled up. The story depends on the government keeping ethanol allocations and prices high while grain stays affordable.
pe_case: Thesis: ~6x TTM earnings, the best cash conversion in the group (FY26 CFO ~1.9x PAT), with assets that would cost far more to replace. Value levers: feedstock flexibility (maize vs FCI rice), sorbitol recovery, and possible move into SAF or bio-CNG. Exit: sale of distillery assets to an integrated sugar or energy group. Must-do diligence: OMC allocation outlook beyond E20, feedstock contracts, and environmental clearances.

name: Crizac
lynch: Fast grower facing a cyclical threat
story: Crizac is a middleman platform: thousands of education agents send student applications through it to UK universities, and it earns a commission on each enrolment. FY26 profit rose 41% as it took share. But 97% of revenue is from the UK, and UK visa rules decide its volumes; Q1 FY27 revenue already fell 4%.
pe_case: Thesis: an asset-light, cash-generative platform at ~12x. Value levers: diversify to Europe, Ireland and Asia-Pacific destinations, add student-finance and accommodation products, and integrate the Global Tree acquisition. Exit: a strategic buyer such as a global education-services group. Must-do diligence: UK policy scenarios (fee levy, Graduate Route), university commission trends, and agent-compliance record.

name: Jeena Sikho Lifecare
story: Jeena Sikho runs Ayurveda hospitals and clinics (HiiMS) where patients get Panchakarma and traditional treatment. Revenue grew 71% and profit 178% because Ayurveda beds are cheap to set up and the brand is pulling in private patients. The story works if patients keep paying and the claims it makes stay on the right side of regulators.
pe_case: Thesis: the only scaled, listed organised-Ayurveda chain, at ~17x versus hospitals at ~31x. Value levers: clinical-outcome documentation to defend pricing and insurance cover, standardised protocols for scaling, and the UAE/international expansion. Exit: wellness and healthcare PE funds or hospital groups adding an AYUSH vertical. Must-do diligence: revenue mix (cash vs government panel), lease-adjusted EBITDA, FCF conversion and advertising compliance.

name: KP Green Engineering
industry: Electronic and Other Electrical Equipment and Components, except Computer Equipment
story: KP Green fabricates transmission towers and solar mounting structures, largely for its own KP Group sister companies building wind and solar parks. Revenue grew 79% because the group and the national grid are both spending heavily. The story works if it wins enough outside customers to stand on its own.
pe_case: Thesis: ~10x earnings with a Rs 1,800+ Cr order book (1.5x revenue). Value levers: grow non-group revenue, migrate from SME to main board, and refinance debt (D/E 1.35). Exit: main-board re-rating or sale to a transmission EPC group. Must-do diligence: related-party revenue share and pricing, receivables owed by group companies, and why TTM profit is below FY26.

name: Apcotex Industries
story: Apcotex makes synthetic latex and rubber that end up in paper coatings, carpets, tyre cord and gloves. Profit nearly doubled in FY26 on flat sales because margins recovered from a trough, helped by anti-dumping duties on imports. The story is a margin cycle plus new capacity coming on line.
pe_case: Thesis: a protected domestic producer with net cash, adding Rs 210 Cr of capacity. Value levers: fill new capacity with exports, and move toward higher-margin specialty grades. Exit: strategic sale to a global latex group. Must-do diligence: anti-dumping duty expiry dates, Chinese price trends and capacity-utilisation ramp.

name: Arrow Greentech
story: Arrow makes water-soluble and biodegradable films (think detergent pods) and anti-counterfeit security products. FY26 was a bad year: revenue fell 18% as government security orders dried up, while the green-film business grew 52%. The story is a turnaround: green films keep growing and security orders come back.
pe_case: Thesis: patented specialty films with a 30%+ ROCE and no debt. Value levers: scale Green into consumer-goods and agrochemical packaging (EPR rules help), and smooth the lumpy security business. Exit: a global specialty-films buyer. Must-do diligence: confirm the Q1 FY27 rebound in filings, Green customer list and repeat rates, and patent strength.

name: Savita Oil Technologies
story: Savita is India's leading maker of transformer oil and white oils, plus the Savsol lubricant brand. FY26 profit rose 61%, and Q1 FY27 brought a one-off windfall from base-oil prices. The steady part of the story is transformer oil riding the grid build-out; the rest swings with crude.
pe_case: Thesis: the transformer-oil leader in a multi-year grid capex cycle. Value levers: grow the Savsol brand, expand in specialty oils, and use the cash buffer. Exit: limited (promoter-controlled); a strategic sale is unlikely. Must-do diligence: normalised margins, and the swap ratio and terms of the promoter-entity merger.

name: TAC Infosec
story: TAC sells cybersecurity software that finds weaknesses in company networks and puts a rupee value on the risk. Revenue grew 88% to Rs 57 Cr, helped by two big partner deals. The story works only if those one-off wins turn into recurring subscriptions.
pe_case: Thesis: a profitable (54% EBITDA) Indian SaaS company with global partners. Value levers: build recurring ARR, add a direct enterprise sales team, and pursue US market entry. Exit: a sale to a global security vendor, or main-board migration. Must-do diligence: ARR and net retention, partner concentration, and collection terms.

name: Unified Data- Tech Solutions
story: Unified Data-Tech installs and maintains IT infrastructure for banks and companies. Revenue grew 31% but profit only 19% as margins slipped, and management now wants to sell safety equipment too. That suggests the core business has run out of easy reinvestment.
pe_case: Thesis: a 35% ROCE integrator at ~17x. Value levers: shift mix toward AMC/managed services, and stop the unrelated diversification. Exit: sale to a larger integrator, or SME migration. Must-do diligence: AMC renewal rates, OEM dependency, and capital allocated to the new venture.

name: Krishna Defence and Allied Industries
story: Krishna Defence supplies special steel and fabricated parts for Indian Navy warships. Profit rose 86% as shipbuilding picked up. But its order book covers only five months of revenue, so the story needs new orders soon.
pe_case: Thesis: a qualified naval vendor in an indigenisation programme. Value levers: win corvette and NGMV packages, add new grades, and diversify to submarines and exports. Exit: sale to a defence major. At ~36x the entry price already reflects the theme. Must-do diligence: order pipeline conversion, approvals, and CFO.

name: Modison
story: Modison makes the silver contacts inside electrical switchgear. Demand is strong because the grid is expanding, but most of the recent profit jump came from silver prices rising on its inventory. The story works if switchgear volumes grow faster than silver falls.
pe_case: Thesis: a qualified, sticky component supplier to switchgear OEMs. Value levers: better hedging policy, and price contracts that pass silver through. Exit: a strategic buyer among global contact makers. Must-do diligence: ex-silver profitability, hedge book, and OEM approval list.

name: Modern Insulators
story: Modern Insulators makes porcelain insulators that hold up high-voltage transmission lines, and more than half of its sales are exports. Profit doubled in FY26 and Q1 FY27 profit rose 80%, backed by an order book of roughly Rs 3,400-3,700 Cr (about five years of revenue). The story works if it can expand capacity to execute that book.
pe_case: Thesis: a huge order book versus revenue, in a global grid-capex cycle, at ~28x FY26 and ~18x TTM. Value levers: capacity expansion, export pricing, and cleaning up the pending amalgamation. Exit: a strategic sale to a global insulator maker. Must-do diligence: the reason for the qualified FY26 audit opinion, amalgamation terms, and capacity constraints.

name: Sathlokhar Synergys E&C Global
story: Sathlokhar is a Tamil Nadu building and solar EPC contractor. Revenue roughly doubled in FY26, and H1 FY27 revenue nearly doubled again (Rs 502 Cr vs Rs 271 Cr) with profit more than doubling. The story works if it keeps winning orders (Rs 1,139 Cr book) and gets paid on time.
pe_case: Thesis: ~11x FY26 earnings on a business growing ~100%. Value levers: SME-to-main-board migration, wider geographic footprint, and working-capital funding. Exit: main-board re-rating. Must-do diligence: receivables and CFO, client concentration, and why the promoter stake fell ~4pp.

name: Univastu India
story: Univastu is a small civil contractor for municipal and public infrastructure in Maharashtra (water, roads, buildings). FY26 revenue rose 42% and profit 66%, and its order book (~Rs 1,854 Cr) is about 7x revenue. The story is about executing that book without running out of working capital.
pe_case: Thesis: a micro-cap with an order book many times its revenue. Value levers: equity or working-capital funding to execute faster, and better contract terms. Exit: re-rating as execution shows. Must-do diligence: municipal payment record, order-book quality (signed vs L1), and CFO.

name: Khazanchi Jewellers
story: Khazanchi is a Chennai gold and diamond jewellery wholesaler that is moving into retail (it opened a 10,000 sq ft flagship). FY26 profit doubled on 16% revenue growth, partly from margin and inventory gains as gold prices rose. The story works if the retail push lifts margins durably.
pe_case: Thesis: a wholesaler-to-retailer shift targeting Rs 5,000 Cr revenue and 40% retail by 2030. Value levers: retail store rollout and brand building. Exit: consolidation in organised jewellery retail. Must-do diligence: inventory and gold-loan exposure, and CFO (Q3 FY25 operating cash was tiny).

name: Tinna Rubber and Infrastructure
story: Tinna recycles old tyres into crumb rubber, rubber-modified bitumen for roads and steel wire. Tyre-recycling rules (EPR) and road-building specs push demand its way. FY26 revenue grew ~8% but Q1 FY27 profit rose 75%, and capacity is going from 185k to 235k tonnes.
pe_case: Thesis: a regulatory-tailwind recycler (EPR for end-of-life tyres) with expanding capacity. Value levers: EPR credit monetisation, export (Oman plant reaching breakeven), and higher-value products. Exit: strategic sale to a tyre or road-materials group. Must-do diligence: EPR enforcement, feedstock costs, and Oman profitability.

name: Accent Microcell
story: Accent makes microcrystalline cellulose, the inert powder that holds pharmaceutical tablets together, and sells about 63% of it abroad. FY26 revenue grew 32% and profit 33%, but its new Unit-III plant is delayed and an independent director has resigned.
pe_case: Thesis: a niche pharma-excipient exporter with premium-product upgrades. Value levers: commission the new plant, add higher-margin grades (MCC spheres, CCS). Exit: strategic sale to a global excipient group. Must-do diligence: plant approval status, traded vs manufactured revenue, and the director's resignation reason.

name: Supreme Power Equipment
story: Supreme Power makes distribution and power transformers for discoms and renewable projects. H1 FY27 income grew ~80% and profit 45%, and the order book of Rs 566 Cr is several times revenue. The story is a small transformer maker riding the same grid boom as bigger rivals.
pe_case: Thesis: a small transformer maker with verified cash conversion (FY25 CFO 1.6x profit) and a large order book. Value levers: capacity expansion and higher-rating transformers. Exit: main-board migration or a strategic sale. Must-do diligence: FY26 audited numbers (estimated here), discom receivables, and raw-material (CRGO steel) pass-through.

name: Advait Energy Transitions
story: Advait supplies transmission-line equipment and renewable EPC, and is building a green-hydrogen electrolyser business. FY26 revenue rose 80% and profit 75%, H1 FY27 profit rose 78%, and the order book is Rs 1,575 Cr (over 2x revenue).
pe_case: Thesis: a grid and renewables EPC company with a green-hydrogen option. Value levers: execute the transmission book, and prove electrolyser economics. Exit: sale to an energy-transition major. Must-do diligence: green-hydrogen capex commitments, and order-book margins.

name: Bondada Engineering
industry: Heavy Construction Other Than Building Construction Contractors
story: Bondada builds solar plants, battery-storage systems and telecom tower infrastructure. FY26 revenue rose 81% to ~Rs 2,843 Cr and profit 86% to ~Rs 211 Cr, and its order book of ~Rs 7,875 Cr is nearly three years of revenue (with a further Rs 9,000 Cr Andhra Pradesh solar order not yet counted).
pe_case: Thesis: solar and storage EPC at ~14x with a very large book. Value levers: execute the book, move into IPP (owning assets), and manage working capital. Exit: re-rating as execution shows, or a sale to an energy group. Must-do diligence: order-book quality (signed vs LoI), counterparty credit, and CFO trend.

name: PIX Transmissions
story: PIX makes industrial V-belts sold worldwide through subsidiaries in the UAE, UK and Germany. FY26 was flat to slightly down on margin pressure, but Q1 FY27 profit nearly doubled. It is a steady, cash-generative export manufacturer, not a high-growth story.
pe_case: Thesis: a global niche belt brand with verified cash conversion. Value levers: pricing, product range (synthetic and power-transmission belts), and distribution. Exit: a strategic sale to a global power-transmission group. Must-do diligence: what drove the Q1 FY27 jump (one-offs vs pricing), and export-market demand.
